name: Sheru Bhai - Golden Lion Boss
visual_dna: Anthropomorphic golden-maned lion, upright, broad shoulders, calm unimpressed face
Crisp white three-piece suit, grey waistcoat, gold aviator sunglasses, thick gold chain
Lavish Indian mansion entrance: marble floor, brass lamps, sweeping staircase, warm rim light
Slow-motion entrance walk toward camera, low hero angle, dust motes in sunbeams
Signature beat: lowers aviators with one finger, stares down the mistake
Hard cut from luxury slow-mo to a flat, bright 'fix card' with the exact spec
character_sheet_prompt: Single full-frame vertical 9:16 cinematic hero shot (not a reference sheet, no labels, no text) of an original anthropomorphic golden lion boss character, upright human posture, full golden mane, wearing a crisp white three-piece suit with grey waistcoat, gold aviator sunglasses and a thick gold chain, standing in a lavish Indian mansion foyer with marble floor and brass lamps, warm cinematic rim light, confident unimpressed expression, stylised 3D animation look, clean background separation, no text, no logos
audio_vibe: Heavy slow-motion boss-entrance drum hits (original, not a copyrighted track), bass drop on the aviator lower, deep calm Indian-English voice with Kannada/Hindi asides; silence right before the punchline
hook_formula: 0-1.5 s: slow-mo boss walk-in + a tiny 'wrong' object in frame (wrong washer, missing bracket). Sheru stops, lowers aviators. Caption pops: the mistake in 3 words.
reusable_broll_prompts: 9:16 slow-motion shot: original golden lion boss character in a white three-piece suit and gold aviators walking toward camera through a marble Indian mansion foyer, warm rim light, dust motes, cinematic, loopable 4 seconds
9:16 close-up: golden lion boss lowers gold aviator sunglasses with one finger and stares into camera, unimpressed, shallow depth of field, mansion bokeh background
9:16 medium shot: golden lion boss seated on a carved wooden throne-like chair, tapping a gold pen on a clipboard, slow push-in
retention_psychology: Status inversion (an absurd luxury boss cares intensely about a tiny technical detail) creates surprise; the aviator-lower is a ritual beat that becomes a Pavlovian 'mistake incoming' cue; the punchline is attached to the exact spec, so recalling the joke recalls the number.
teaching_fit: wrong choice -> boss punishment -> correct spec
safety_notes: Original character only: never depict a real person, celebrity or a specific existing film character
No real brand logos on suits, watches or products
Punchlines mock the mistake, never the learner's background, caste, region, accent or gender
